THE GREAT FOREST / CELESTEVILLE

CELESTEVILLE · BORDER COMMAND

The Siege of
Celesteville.

Rataxes’s columns have crossed the border. Keep the palace supplied, hold the forest approaches, and break his fortress before the town falls.

1 Gather and deliver supplies. Recruit guards, scouts, and field artillery.

2 Raid gatherers and seize the central depot. Use cover and withdraw the wounded.

3 Consult the Family & council. Their support can keep the defense alive.

Mouse or touch · Single player · Use the minimap to explore

THE FAMILY BEHIND THE DEFENSE

33 characters: the central book family, friends and adventure guests, alongside the original television, Badou and film roster. Book labels identify representative appearances. Powers and wartime roles are invented. Children provide civilian support; archive characters do not enter combat.

Field manual

Protect the palace and destroy Rataxes’s fortress in the northeast. Choose Story for more time to recover or Commander for stronger, faster assaults.

Supplies: each cache has two extraction slots. Extra workers queue for a slot; spread them across caches. Provisioners collect physical caches and deliver to a supplied palace or home. Buildings connect within 360m. Enemy soldiers within 85m of a link cut it: isolated training runs at 25%. Clear raiders or build connecting homes. A provisioner’s Repair order costs 0.3 supplies per health.

Materials: build a Materials Quarry (100 Supplies) on a blue deposit, then select provisioners and Gather there. Three workers can extract at once. Cargo must reach a supplied palace or home to enter your stockpile. A quarry needs a supply link; raiders or its destruction stop extraction. Materials fund advanced production: Artillery Works costs 240 Supplies + 50 Materials and needs a completed Guard School; each gun costs 160 Supplies + 25 Materials; shell research costs 180 Supplies + 60 Materials. The central deposit supports expansion. Rhino guns also consume physically gathered Materials.

Macro commands: I or Idle selects waiting provisioners. Select multiple production buildings and recruit repeatedly to use the shortest available queue. Researching, unfinished, destroyed and full buildings are skipped. Recruitment cancellation refunds both resources in full; cancelled construction and research return 75% of each.

Phone: tap a friendly unit to select it, then tap open ground to move or an enemy to focus fire. Tap a building, then Build / train to recruit; use Production to choose a site and set its rally with a map tap. Two fingers pan/zoom. Army / move closes the expanded panel. More orders contains specialist commands. Menu contains pause, sound, family and the field manual. Only leaving the app/tab automatically pauses play.

H-bomb: after Atomic command, research H-bomb command at Artillery Works for 1000 Supplies + 350 Materials and 120s. Assembly costs another 1000 Supplies + 350 Materials and 110 supplied seconds. It has a larger 230m blast and 28s warning. Both types share one payload slot per faction. Existing bombs stay atomic; choose which type to assemble. Evacuation, launcher destruction, supply disruption and friendly fire still apply.

Atomic command: both sides can research this at Artillery Works after Calibrated field shells and Field protection II. Research costs 800 Supplies + 300 Materials and 90s. Assemble one bomb for 650 Supplies + 200 Materials and 75 supplied seconds. Select the Works → Launch → tap a visible target. Everyone sees an 18-second warning and a 150m blast circle; friendly fire applies. Evacuate or destroy/isolate the launching Works to abort (payload is lost). Targets stay fixed after launch. Rhinos use the same costs and only target currently visible forces.

Munitions: start with 24, maximum 100. Owning the central depot earns 0.5 per second; enemy soldiers within 90m interrupt it. A supplied Guard School or Artillery Works can pack 20 for 60 Supplies and 20 Materials, once per 30 seconds per workshop. Select troops → Build / skills: Heavy rounds costs 8 per eligible unit for +50% damage over 15 seconds; Smoke cover costs 6 per eligible unit for 25% less incoming damage over 12 seconds. Payment is all-or-nothing for the eligible selection. Active effects cannot be stacked or refreshed. Normal attacks never require Munitions. Rhino occupation denies this command reserve while earning their normal depot Supplies.

Depot: hold the central depot with soldiers for 8 uncontested seconds. It grants 2 Supplies per second to its owner. Rhino workers physically gather and deliver the rest. Every third assault can detach a small squad against an exposed home, quarry or recently seen provisioner. A dedicated rhino scout revisits the approaches and withdraws from visible danger. Replacements cost Supplies and occupy the Guard School; killing scouts or destroying the school denies current intelligence. Known towers and nearby defenders deter raids. Watch both approaches and withdraw threatened workers. Raid workers or cut supply links to starve recruitment. Destroy production to interrupt queues; engineers can rebuild with paid resources. Scout to locate expansion homes.

Construction: placing a structure assigns a free provisioner, preferring selected workers. It only progresses while a builder is on site. If the builder leaves or falls, send another with Repair. Extra builders do not speed up construction. Cancel unfinished structures for a 75% refund.

Missiles: Research Ballistic command at Artillery Works, then build a Ballistic Launcher. Each conventional shot costs 120 Supplies / 40 Materials, has 900m range, a 10s warning and 35s reload. Damage Limitation unlocks Missile Defense Batteries: 260m coverage, 20 Supplies / 10 Materials per interceptor, 12s reload. Keep them supplied. One interceptor stops conventional/atomic missiles; H-bombs need two. Arthur’s neutron payload bypasses ballistic defense.
Nuclear authority: Only Babar can authorize elephant nuclear strikes; Rataxes alone authorizes rhino launches. Select your leader to launch. The leader must personally see a completed friendly Palace/Fortress or Field Headquarters: distance, forest and intervening buildings matter. Scouts and reveal powers cannot substitute. This includes Arthur’s neutron payload.
Civil Defense: First research Austin Long: Damage Limitation at the Guard School (150 Supplies + 50 Materials, 40s). This fictional unlock is inspired by his writing; the shelter effects are original game rules. Then build a shelter (180 Supplies + 80 Materials). Any nuclear launch warning automatically sends provisioners to a completed friendly shelter, preferring one outside the marked blast. Within its 110m perimeter workers take 95% less nuclear damage. No supply link required. Cargo and orders are retained; work resumes 3 seconds after all-clear. Workers without a shelter remain at work.
Uranium: Complete Artillery Works, then assign provisioners to ochre U deposits. Each contains 120 Uranium; two workers can extract 4 units each per 3 seconds and must deliver to a linked base. Atomic assembly costs 40 U; H-bomb assembly costs 80 U. Both factions follow these rules.
Research: an idle Guard School can research Cornelius’s coordinated volleys (150 supplies, 25s, +20% guard/scout/sapper damage). Artillery Works can calibrate shells (180 supplies + 60 materials, 35s, +25% gun damage). Research occupies that building, slows to 25% when isolated, and benefits existing and future troops. Cancellation refunds 75%; destruction loses the project.

Army: guards hold ground and counter sappers; scouts move quickly and see farther; field artillery outranges towers and deals 80% extra damage to buildings. Protect artillery with guards. Field Sappers train at Guard Schools after Artillery Works is complete (90 Supplies, 20 Materials, 10s). Their 170m weapon deals 10 damage against light troops and 30 against armored guns and buildings. Guards beat sappers in a direct fight; scouts spot for artillery. Deploy guns with D or the selection button: 3s setup, 390m range, 90m blind spot, 72 damage with splash that also hits allies. Scouts must spot distant targets. Move, attack-move or Retreat packs the gun for 2s; it cannot fire or move during setup. Mobile guns retain 270m range and 48 damage. Select guns to see readiness, reloads, close threats and friendly-fire risk. Keep infantry ahead and scouts beyond the guns; deploy when spotted targets enter range. Pack forward once the position is clear. Repeated attack-move orders pack deployed guns, so command infantry separately while the battery fires. A friendly-fire warning does not stop a shot. Sandbag cover reduces incoming damage by 35% for either faction.

Rapid advance (V): research coordinated volleys, then Rapid advance doctrine at a Guard School (180 Supplies, 60 Materials, 35s). Selected guards, scouts and sappers spend 20 health for +30% movement speed and 30% shorter firing intervals for 6s. Cooldown is 24s from activation. Requires over 20 health and at least 35 morale. Withdraw to supplied aid stations to recover; the speed bonus does not stack with commander advance.

Hero combat: Babar and Rataxes fight with 24-damage basic attacks at 100m. Select Babar → Build / skills → Fight, then tap an enemy or ground. Fight releases Hold fire. Royal strike (F) spends 35 energy for a 60-damage shot, with a 12s cooldown. It uses the current visible target in range, otherwise the nearest visible enemy in range; armor, cover and protection still apply. No target means no cost. An explicit strike works once while holding fire, preserving that stance. During Retreat, finish withdrawing or give another order first. Energy is shared with Stand together, so choose offense or protection.

Commanders: select Babar and use Stand together (Q): 50 energy, 35s cooldown, +20 morale and 25% less incoming damage for friendly mobile units within 180m for 8s. Commanders start with 60 energy and recover 1.25/s, capped at 100. Rataxes can order a forced advance: nearby units move 30% faster and inflict 6 extra suppression per hit for 8s. His command requires a visible enemy and a supporting formation.

Morale: hits suppress units; below 25 they withdraw automatically. After 3 seconds without fire, morale recovers by 4/s, 12/s near a commander, or 10/s at an aid station. Below 45, movement and firing slow. Retreat moves 20% faster and avoids engagement.

Population: Queued recruits reserve population. Losing homes can put the army over capacity: recruitment pauses when living units fill the cap. Paid queues and progress remain. Build a Village Home or free population to resume; returning commanders also need room. Research continues.

Recovery: linked homes and palaces heal nearby units by 2/s after 5 seconds without fire; Celeste raises this to 6/s. Commanders recover for 45 seconds, then return when 100 supplies are available. Periwinkle reduces the wait to 25 seconds.

Scouting stocks: ? means unscouted; ~ marks a last-seen quantity. Workers automatically switch only to known stocks, and wait idle if none remain. Scout new supplies and give Gather orders to resume.

Fire discipline: select soldiers or commanders and use Hold fire / Weapons free (C). Hold fire prevents automatic shooting and chasing, including during attack-move or patrol. A new focus-fire order overrides the stance for that target only; losing sight or defeating it restores silence. Enabling Hold fire suspends earlier focus-fire orders. Movement routes remain. It does not hide units or stop enemies attacking them. Hold position (S) still allows fire within range unless Hold fire is enabled.

iPhone: use Orders, Build / skills and Unit status tabs below the map. Drag with two fingers to pan and pinch to zoom; lifting your fingers never issues an order. One finger selects or uses your chosen order. Pan map enables one-finger camera movement. Switching apps pauses the battle; tap Resume when ready.

Orders: drag to select; Shift adds units; right-click moves or focuses a visible enemy. A selects attack-move, M move, G gather, E repair, S hold, R retreat. F2 selects the army; F4 opens the live production report, showing queue progress and supply interruptions. T cycles unit-type subgroups (Shift+T reverses). The type buttons isolate units for orders; All restores the retained selection. Selecting units on the map or recalling a control group starts a new selection. H returns to the palace. Shift+F5–F8 saves four camera positions and zoom levels; F5–F8 returns without changing selection or orders. Views offers the same controls on touch. Hold Shift while giving orders, or enable Queue on touch, to append up to 16 waypoints. Hold and Retreat cancel the route. A queued order after gathering starts once the next delivery is complete, or when gathering cannot continue. Select a provisioner and use Shift or Queue when placing buildings to schedule construction. Foundations are paid immediately and remain vulnerable while waiting. Cancel a foundation for a 75% refund; Repair assigns a replacement builder. Ctrl/Command + 0–9 saves a control group; 0–9 recalls it; add Shift when saving to append. Select a production building and right-click (touch: Move then tap) to set its rally point. Rally provisioners to a cache to begin gathering. Space pauses. Touch uses the same explicit order buttons and Pan map. Scroll or +/− zooms. Family & council pauses the simulation; closing it restores the previous pause state.

Control groups

Assign the current selection, then recall it during battle. Fallen units are removed. Command is paused here.
